rv.q: Moss and Jamie Armitage’s infectiously fun production is packed with witty touches that make history, and theatre, easily accessible.

This is quite the most uplifting piece of new British musical theatre I have ever had the privilege to watch and the fact that it comes from two 23-year-olds, Toby Marlow and Lucy Moss, who graduated only last year, is even more delightful.
Long may these witty queens reign over the West End

There's undoubtedly raw talent on display in the writing, and really accomplished vocal performances – but it currently feels undernourished and, even though it runs to just 70 minutes, overlong for what it is.

Do you enjoy the following: puns, parodies, pop music, noise, neon, shiny stuff, shrieking audiences. If you answered no, then SIX isn't for you. If you answered yes, then you're probably already familiar with the show, which went from Edinburgh Fringe to the Tony Awards in only five years.
Six continues to reign supreme in the West End
Indeed, no matter how many of the previous casts you’ve seen, this is the line-up you don’t want to miss.
Six is an absolute joy, it taps into my inner teenage girl – I wish these Queens were here to empower me when I was younger.

If you are looking for a highly entertaining, music filled night at the theatre I would 100% recommend this show to you.
This is a unique, exciting, and fun show that can be consumed repeatedly.

cn.t: Critics hail SIX as an exhilarating, empowering pop concert musical that reimagines Henry VIII's wives as a girl-power phenomenon, praising its infectious energy and outstanding vocals, though some find the concept gimmicky and unconventional.
